q6.answer: Status is stored in the status column of the new report_exports table (queued, running, done, failed), in the application database. The page learns of changes by calling GET /api/reports/{report_id}/exports/latest on load, which returns the user's latest export from the last 7 days, and by polling it every 5 s while queued or running. A later return to the report just reads the same row.

q7.answer: It streams. The job pages through the replica 5,000 rows at a time by keyset, appends CSV bytes to an 8 MB buffer, and uploads each full buffer as a multipart part, then empties the buffer. Memory stays at one buffer, one page and the etag list, tens of MB. About 115 parts for 900 MB, within the 10,000-part limit. It sets its own deadline of about 1,700 s, under the 1,800 s attempt timeout.

q8.answer: The data is invisible: nothing shows at the key until complete_multipart. On an error the attempt calls abort_multipart and re-raises. If the worker dies or times out, the bucket's 24-hour rule discards the orphan parts. The queue keeps no progress, so the next attempt restarts from the very beginning with a new multipart upload to the same key.

q9.answer: They are kept in the filters and cols columns of the report_exports row, inserted at click time. The job payload carries only export_id, and the handler loads the row to get filters, cols, user_id and report_id. That avoids the 64 KB payload limit.

q10.answer: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running'). The insert uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so only one of two simultaneous requests inserts a row. The loser selects and returns the existing export.

q11.answer: The file must be fully uploaded and complete_multipart must have succeeded. The row must also be updated to done (only WHERE status='running'). The link is signed at send time. If the job runs again, it loads the row: if done with notified_at null it sends only the email. If done with notified_at set it returns. If failed it returns. So a duplicate run produces one file and one email, apart from a rare duplicate if notified_at failed to save.

q12.answer: Nothing is written to the database or storage, and nothing is sent until the whole CSV is built in memory. A failure or the 45 s deadline gives a clean 500 (with an 'Export took too long, try again' message for the deadline), never a truncated 200. The user can click again.
